items.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon, topping Artificial Analysis Index v5 and pitched at cybersecurity and long-horizon agents
items.summary: Two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon, Google DeepMind announced Gemini 4 Carbon as its most capable model, with 'significant gains' in coding, agentic tasks and cybersecurity. Google says it ranks first on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 (score 59, per IT之家), ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra (The Verge). IT之家 reports introductory API pricing of $2 per million input and $10 per million output tokens, rising to $4/$20 after the introductory period, with a 95% discount on cached input, and a 1,769 score (4th) on WebDev Arena, up 89 Elo. Ars Technica notes that, like Argon, Carbon is on a staged release that could take a while.
items.why_it_matters: A new top-of-index frontier model at the same entry price as Argon pressures OpenAI and Anthropic on price-performance, and Google is leaning on cyber-defence capability as the differentiator. Access is staged, so developers may not be able to use it yet.

An $8.7 billion equity-investment loss cut after-tax profit by about $6.7B, or $0.55 a share. items.why_it_matters: The first of the big-tech AI earnings to read negatively: revenue and Cloud growth were strong, yet the market punished the earnings miss and the ad shortfall, feeding the 'AI capex vs returns' debate.

items.title: Artificial Analysis Index v5 adds 60% private test sets and FrontierCode 2.0; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash leads open models
items.summary: Artificial Analysis released Intelligence Index v5, its biggest rebuild since v4 in January, per IT之家: 60% of weighting now rests on private or hidden-answer test sets to limit training-data contamination. Coding carries 25%, of which Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0 (132 real open-source tasks scored by maintainers on whether they would merge the PR) takes 15% and Terminal-Bench 4.0 10%. IT之家's headline says DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 posts the best open-model score on FrontierCode 2.0. Nathan Lambert's Interconnects post discusses the 'benchmarker's dilemma' of choosing what to hill-climb.
items.why_it_matters: The index is the scoreboard labs now cite at launch (Google leads with it today), so a shift towards merge-ability and hidden test sets changes what 'best model' means.

items.summary: At GitHub Universe, EVP Jay Parikh announced the 2026 Octoverse report.
